text: Project Layout¶
label: unreviewed

text: Create a project directory and enter it:
label: unreviewed

text: $ mkdir flask-tutorial $ cd flask-tutorial
label: unreviewed

text: Then follow the installation instructions to set up a Python virtual environment and install Flask for your project.
label: unreviewed

text: The tutorial will assume you’re working from the flask-tutorial directory from now on. The file names at the top of each code block are relative to this directory.
label: unreviewed

text: A Flask application can be as simple as a single file.
label: unreviewed

text: from flask import Flask app = Flask(__name__) @app.route('/') def hello(): return 'Hello, World!'
label: unreviewed

text: However, as a project gets bigger, it becomes overwhelming to keep all the code in one file. Python projects use packages to organize code into multiple modules that can be imported where needed, and the tutorial will do this as well.
label: unreviewed

text: The project directory will contain:
label: unreviewed

text: flaskr/, a Python package containing your application code and files.
label: unreviewed

text: flaskr/, a Python package containing your application code and files.
label: unreviewed

text: tests/, a directory containing test modules.
label: unreviewed

text: tests/, a directory containing test modules.
label: unreviewed

text: .venv/, a Python virtual environment where Flask and other dependencies are installed.
label: unreviewed

text: .venv/, a Python virtual environment where Flask and other dependencies are installed.
label: unreviewed

text: Installation files telling Python how to install your project.
label: unreviewed

text: Installation files telling Python how to install your project.
label: unreviewed

text: Version control config, such as git. You should make a habit of using some type of version control for all your projects, no matter the size.
label: unreviewed

text: By the end, your project layout will look like this:
label: unreviewed

text: /home/user/Projects/flask-tutorial ├── flaskr/ │ ├── __init__.py │ ├── db.py │ ├── schema.sql │ ├── auth.py │ ├── blog.py │ ├── templates/ │ │ ├── base.html │ │ ├── auth/ │ │ │ ├── login.html │ │ │ └── register.html │ │ └── blog/ │ │ ├── create.html │ │ ├── index.html │ │ └── update.html │ └── static/ │ └── style.css ├── tests/ │ ├── conftest.py │ ├── data.sql │ ├── test_factory.py │ ├── test_db.py │ ├── test_auth.py │ └── test_blog.py ├── .venv/ ├── pyproject.toml └── MANIFEST.in
label: unreviewed

text: If you’re using version control, the following files that are generated while running your project should be ignored. There may be other files based on the editor you use. In general, ignore files that you didn’t write. For example, with git:
label: unreviewed

text: .venv/ *.pyc __pycache__/ instance/ .pytest_cache/ .coverage htmlcov/ dist/ build/ *.egg-info/
